items.title: Bob Stewart interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006
items.q: sometimes Kenny Dorham came in and sat in with the band

ctx.x: Who did you have a dashiki with?

This was early in New York in the late sixties, early seventies, when the call for dress in a lot of the jazz bands during that period that weren’t necessarily in the mainstream was dashiki, and this particular band was Collective Black Artists Big Band. And it was a big band that was under the auspices of Reggie Workman and people like Buster Williams and sometimes Kenny Dorham came in and sat in with the band and Frank Foster was there and Charlie Persip, drummer. And this was an organization that was the…
And early on it looked like you moved around as a child? I just was reading a little bio about you and you were born in South Dakota but you didn’t stay there?
